title: V'Zot HaBerachah: an inheritance (Deuteronomy 33:4)
hookLine: the Torah is "the inheritance of the congregation of Jacob", learned from childhood

lines: A RHYME, A PLEDGE, A SONG.
cards: What's the first sentence you remember learning by heart? A nursery rhyme, a prayer at bedtime, a pledge at school, a line from a song. Whatever it was, it may still be in there, word for word.
The Talmud says that when a Jewish child first begins to talk, there's a particular verse a parent should teach. It isn't from Genesis, at the beginning of everything.
It's from the very end of the Torah, tucked in among Moses' blessings.

teach.b: "Moses commanded us a law, An inheritance of the congregation of Jacob." In Hebrew: Torah tzivah lanu Moshe, morashah kehillat Ya'akov.
The Talmud, in Sukkah, says that as soon as a child can speak, the father teaches him this verse, along with the first line of the Shema. Notice the little word lanu, to us.
A child's first verse already says we. Now the second half. Morashah, inheritance.
And whose inheritance is it? Not the priests'. Not the scholars'.
The congregation of Jacob: everyone. Maimonides makes the point sharply.

teach.h: THREE CROWNS, ONE OPEN TO ALL.
teach.b: Israel was given three crowns, he writes. The crown of priesthood went to Aaron's family. The crown of kingship went to David's line.
But the crown of Torah is set out for anyone who wants it: whoever wishes may come and take it. The Talmud also plays with the word.
It reads morashah, inheritance, as if it said me'orasah, betrothed: the Torah isn't only handed down like property; it's meant to be loved.
And some teachers notice that Hebrew has two words for inheritance. Yerushah is what you receive. Morashah, they suggest, is a heritage you hold in order to pass it on.
Either way, the first verse a child learns says: this belongs to you, and to all of us.

how: Following the Talmud, the verse 'Torah tzivah lanu Moshe' is traditionally among the first a young child learns, often sung, together with the first line of the Shema.

o: and this is the song: Moses' poem to the sky
and this is the law: the rules for the priests
and this is the blessing: Moses' last words

games.q: inside the inheritance — tap the pairs.
p: the verse a child learns first
open to anyone who wants it

s: the Talmud's first verse for a child is the opening of Genesis
it names Deuteronomy 33:4, with the first line of the Shema.
Maimonides says the crown of Torah is open to all
priesthood and kingship are inherited; Torah is for whoever wants it.

games.q: Israel has three crowns: priesthood, kingship and Torah. which one, Maimonides says, can anyone at all take up?
games.why: the crown of Torah: 'whoever wishes may come and take it'. the inheritance of the whole congregation.

practice: Choose a short line: this verse, if you like, Moses commanded us a law, an inheritance of the congregation of Jacob, or any line from these weeks that has stayed with you.
Say it once, close your eyes, and say it again without looking; notice which word slips, and go back for it.

wordCard.voice: V'Zot HaBerachah. And this is the blessing. And in it, morashah: an inheritance for the whole congregation.

carryVoice: Your line: inheritance for everyone. Whoever wishes may come and take it. Day five hundred thirty-three.
